BRICS **BRICS** is an [international organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_organization "International organization") currently comprising ten countries: Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-brics2026-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-2) Its conceptual origins were articulated by Russian foreign minister [Yevgeny Primakov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yevgeny_Primakov "Yevgeny Primakov") in 1998, and can be traced to informal forums and dialogue groups such as RIC (Russia, India, and China) and [IBSA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBSA_Dialogue_Forum "IBSA Dialogue Forum") (India, Brazil, and South Africa).[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:3-3) [BRIC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRIC_(economics_term) "BRIC (economics term)") was originally a term coined by British economist [Jim O'Neill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_O'Neill,_Baron_O'Neill_of_Gatley "Jim O'Neill, Baron O'Neill of Gatley"), and later championed by his employer [Goldman Sachs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldman_Sachs "Goldman Sachs") in 2001, to designate a group of emerging markets.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-Rana_Foroohar-4)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-AY-5) The bloc's [inaugural summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_BRIC_summit "1st BRIC summit") was held in 2009 and featured the founding countries of Brazil, Russia, India, and China;[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:0-6) they adopted the [acronym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acronym "Acronym") **BRIC** and formed an informal diplomatic group where their governments could meet annually at formal summits and coordinate multilateral policies.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-OR-7)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-8) South Africa joined the organization in September 2010, which was then renamed BRICS, and attended the [third summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3rd_BRICS_summit "3rd BRICS summit") in 2011 as a full member.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-10) Iran, Egypt, Ethiopia, and the United Arab Emirates attended their first summit as member states [in 2024 in Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16th_BRICS_summit "16th BRICS summit").[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-GI-11) Indonesia officially joined in early 2025, becoming the first [Southeast Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Asia "Southeast Asia") member.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-Reuters-1-12)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-13) Saudi Arabia was invited at the [Johannesburg summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15th_BRICS_summit "15th BRICS summit") and it is considered part of the organisation, but has not publicly confirmed its membership.[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-14) The term **BRICS+** has been informally used to reflect new membership since 2024.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-GI-11)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-BE-15)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-16) Collectively, BRICS comprises more than a quarter of the global economy and nearly half the world's population.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-auto-17) The group has established multilateral institutions and financial mechanisms, such as the [New Development Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Development_Bank "New Development Bank"), the [BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS_Contingent_Reserve_Arrangement "BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement"), and the [BRICS PAY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS_PAY "BRICS PAY") payment platform.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-18)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-19) It has also promoted [de-dollarization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De-dollarization "De-dollarization") initiatives to increase trade settlements in national currencies.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-20)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-FF-21) Some commentators consider BRICS the alternative to the [G7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G7 "G7"),[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-BE-15) and a major political force in the global international order.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-auto-17) Others describe it as an incoherent affiliation of disparate countries centered on increasing [anti-European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Europeanism "Anti-Europeanism") and [anti-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Americanism "Anti-Americanism") objectives.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-22) Nevertheless, all five original members, as well as Indonesia, are also part of the [G20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G20 "G20"). BRICS has received both praise and criticism from numerous commentators and world leaders.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-23)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-USINPAC-24)[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-25)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-Coughlin-26)[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-27) ## History ### Founding Collective action in the political arena in the late 1990s was present before the economic rationale of BRICS.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-28) The idea of a multipolar group like BRICS can be traced back to [Yevgeny Primakov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yevgeny_Primakov "Yevgeny Primakov") during his term as [Minister of Foreign Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Foreign_Affairs_(Russia) "Minister of Foreign Affairs (Russia)") of Russia. He reiterated the idea in New Delhi in 1998.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:3-3) The forums RIC (Russia, India, China) and [IBSA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBSA_Dialogue_Forum "IBSA Dialogue Forum") (India, Brazil, South Africa) predated and played an important role in the creation of BRIC and subsequently BRICS.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:3-3) [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/New_Development_Bank_HQ_Shanghai.jpg/250px-New_Development_Bank_HQ_Shanghai.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:New_Development_Bank_HQ_Shanghai.jpg) The [New Development Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Development_Bank "New Development Bank"), headquartered in [Shanghai, China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai,_China "Shanghai, China"), is the premier institution of BRICS.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-BA-29) The term _[BRIC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRIC_(economics_term) "BRIC (economics term)")_, as compared to the alternate term _CRIB_,[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:0-6) was originally developed in the context of foreign investment strategies. It was introduced in the 2001 publication, _Building Better Global Economic BRICs_ by [Jim O'Neill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_O'Neill,_Baron_O'Neill_of_Gatley "Jim O'Neill, Baron O'Neill of Gatley"), then head of global economics research at [Goldman Sachs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldman_Sachs "Goldman Sachs") and later Chairman of Goldman Sachs Asset Management.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-30)[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-31)[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-32) O'Neill now regards the BRICS group as a failed project. In a 2021 article for _[Project Syndicate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Syndicate "Project Syndicate")_ he wrote that the BRICS countries "have so far proven incapable of uniting as a meaningful global force" and felt in 2024 that "each year also brings further confirmation that the grouping serves no real purpose beyond generating symbolic gestures and lofty rhetoric".[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-PM24-33)[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-PM21-34) The [foreign ministers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_minister "Foreign minister") of the initial four BRIC states (Brazil, Russia, India, and China) met in New York City in September 2006 at the margins of the General Debate of the UN Assembly, beginning a series of high-level meetings.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-35) A full-scale diplomatic meeting was held in [Yekaterinburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yekaterinburg "Yekaterinburg"), Russia, on 16 June 2009.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-36) The BRIC group's [first formal summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_BRIC_summit "1st BRIC summit"), also held in Yekaterinburg, commenced on 16 June 2009,[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-BBC-37) with [Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_In%C3%A1cio_Lula_da_Silva "Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva"), [Dmitry Medvedev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dmitry_Medvedev "Dmitry Medvedev"), [Manmohan Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manmohan_Singh "Manmohan Singh"), and [Hu Jintao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hu_Jintao "Hu Jintao"), the respective leaders of Brazil, Russia, India, and China, all attending.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-reuters-38) The summit's focus was on improving the global economic situation and reforming [financial institutions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_institution "Financial institution") amid the [Great Recession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Recession "Great Recession"). There was also discussion of how the four countries could better cooperate in the future,[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-BBC-37)[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-reuters-38) and ways [developing countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developing_country "Developing country"), such as three-fourths of the BRIC members, could become more involved in global affairs.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-reuters-38) In the aftermath of the 2009 Yekaterinburg summit, the BRIC nations announced the need for a new [global reserve currency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_currency "World currency"), which would have to be "diverse, stable and predictable".[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-39) Although their statement did not directly criticize the perceived dominance of the [US dollar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar") (as Russia had in the past) it did spark a fall in the value of the dollar against other major currencies.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-40) ### 2010 expansion In 2010, South Africa began efforts to join BRIC, and the process for its formal admission began in August of that year.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-foreignpolicyjournal.com-41) South Africa officially became a member nation on 24 December 2010 after being formally invited by China,[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-42) and was subsequently accepted by other BRIC countries.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-foreignpolicyjournal.com-41) The group was renamed _BRICS_ to represent the addition of _South Africa_ to the original four BRIC members.[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-43) At the [third BRICS summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3rd_BRICS_summit "3rd BRICS summit") in 2011 in [Sanya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanya "Sanya"), China, South African president [Jacob Zuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Zuma "Jacob Zuma") represented the country as a full member for the first time.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-44)[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-45)[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-46) ### New Development Bank [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/NDB-HQ-LOGO.jpg/250px-NDB-HQ-LOGO.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NDB-HQ-LOGO.jpg) New Development Bank's logo[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/PM_in_a_family_photograph_during_the_BRICS_Leaders_Retreat_Meeting%2C_at_Johannesburg%2C_in_South_Africa_on_August_23%2C_2023_%281%29.jpg/250px-PM_in_a_family_photograph_during_the_BRICS_Leaders_Retreat_Meeting%2C_at_Johannesburg%2C_in_South_Africa_on_August_23%2C_2023_%281%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PM_in_a_family_photograph_during_the_BRICS_Leaders_Retreat_Meeting,_at_Johannesburg,_in_South_Africa_on_August_23,_2023_(1).jpg) South African President [Cyril Ramaphosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyril_Ramaphosa "Cyril Ramaphosa") and other BRICS representatives during the [15th BRICS summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15th_BRICS_summit "15th BRICS summit") in Johannesburg, 23 August 2023 In June 2012, the BRICS nations pledged $75billion to boost the lending power of the [International Monetary Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund "International Monetary Fund") (IMF). However, the proposed loan was conditional on IMF voting reforms.[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-47) In March 2013, during the [fifth BRICS summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5th_BRICS_summit "5th BRICS summit") in [Durban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durban "Durban"), the member countries agreed to create a global financial institution to cooperate with the western-dominated IMF and World Bank.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-48) They planned to set up this [New Development Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Development_Bank "New Development Bank") (known at the time as the "BRICS Development Bank") by 2014.[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-49) At the BRICS leaders meeting in [Saint Petersburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Petersburg "Saint Petersburg") in September 2013, China committed $41billion towards the pool; Brazil, India, and Russia committed $18 billion each; and South Africa committed $5 billion. China, which held the world's largest foreign exchange reserves and contributed the bulk of the currency pool, wanted a more significant managing role. China also wanted to be the location of the reserve.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-50) In October 2013, Russia's Finance Minister [Anton Siluanov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anton_Siluanov "Anton Siluanov") said that creating a $100billion in funds designated to steady currency markets would be taken in early 2014. The Brazilian finance minister, [Guido Mantega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guido_Mantega "Guido Mantega"), confirmed that the fund would be created by March 2014.[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-51) However, by April 2014, the currency reserve pool and development bank had yet to be set up, and the date was rescheduled to 2015.[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-rbth1-52) In July 2014, during the [sixth BRICS summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/6th_BRICS_summit "6th BRICS summit") in [Fortaleza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortaleza "Fortaleza"), the BRICS members signed a document to create the US$100billion New Development Bank and a reserve currency pool worth over another US$100billion. Documents on cooperation between BRICS export credit agencies and an agreement of cooperation on innovation were also signed.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-53) The Fortaleza summit was followed by a BRICS meeting with the [Union of South American Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_of_South_American_Nations "Union of South American Nations") presidents in [Brasília](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bras%C3%ADlia "Brasília").[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-yn11j-54) ### Other initiatives [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0b/2024_BRICS_Games_opening_ceremony_31.jpg/250px-2024_BRICS_Games_opening_ceremony_31.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2024_BRICS_Games_opening_ceremony_31.jpg) [2024 BRICS Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_BRICS_Games "2024 BRICS Games") in Russia Since 2011, the National Institutes of Statistics of the BRICS group of countries ( [Institute of Geography and Statistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Institute_of_Geography_and_Statistics "Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics") (Brazil), [Federal State Statistics Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_State_Statistics_Service_(Russia) "Federal State Statistics Service (Russia)") (Russia), the [National Bureau of Statistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Statistics_of_China "National Bureau of Statistics of China") (China), the [Central Statistics Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Statistics_Office_(India) "Central Statistics Office (India)") (India), and [Statistics South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistics_South_Africa "Statistics South Africa") produce an annual joint statistical publication to put statistical production in perspective, compare adopted methodologies and statistical results. The publication serves as a single data platform for the mutual benefit of participating countries. Since 2012, the BRICS group of countries has been planning an [optical fiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_fiber "Optical fiber") [submarine communications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine_communication_cables "Submarine communication cables") cable system to carry telecommunications between the BRICS countries, known as the [BRICS Cable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS_Cable "BRICS Cable").[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-bloomberg-55) Part of the motivation for the project was the spying of the [U.S. National Security Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Agency "National Security Agency") on all telecommunications that flowed in and out of United States territory.[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-diplomat-56) Construction of the proposed cable network was abandoned in 2015, possibly due to cost.[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-57) In August 2019, the communications ministers of the BRICS countries signed a letter of intent to cooperate in the Information and Communication Technology sector. This agreement was signed in the fifth edition of the meeting of communication ministers of countries member of the group[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-58) held in [Brasília](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bras%C3%ADlia "Brasília"), Brazil. [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/9YAN_5350_%2852766002359%29.jpg/250px-9YAN_5350_%2852766002359%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:9YAN_5350_(52766002359).jpg) Meeting of BRICS foreign ministers on 22 September 2022 The [New Development Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Development_Bank "New Development Bank") plans on giving out $15billion to member states to help their struggling economies. Member countries are hoping for a smooth comeback and a continuation of economic trade pre-COVID-19. The 2020 BRICS summit was held virtually in St. Petersburg, Russia, and discussed how to handle the COVID-19 pandemic and how to fix the multilateral system via reforms.[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-59) During the 13th BRICS summit, in 2021, Indian Prime Minister [Narendra Modi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi") called for a transparent investigation into the [origins of COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origins_of_COVID-19 "Origins of COVID-19") under the [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization") with the full cooperation of "all countries", and Chinese leader [Xi Jinping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_Jinping "Xi Jinping") spoke directly afterwards, calling on BRICS countries to "oppose politicisation" of the process.[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-60) In May 2023, South Africa announced that it would be giving [diplomatic immunity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomatic_immunity "Diplomatic immunity") to Vladimir Putin and other Russian officials so that they could attend the 15th BRICS Summit despite the [ICC arrest warrant for Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_arrest_warrants_for_Vladimir_Putin_and_Maria_Lvova-Belova "ICC arrest warrants for Vladimir Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova").[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-61)[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-62) In July 2023, the Russian president announced that he would not personally attend the BRICS summit in Johannesburg on 22–24 August despite good relations with the South African government. Russian news channels noted that Putin would remotely participate online in all BRICS leaders' sessions, including the Business Forum, and also deliver his remarks virtually.[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-63) In the first 15 years of BRICS, it produced hundreds of decisions and complied with a majority of them.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-FF-21) BRICS has established almost 60 intra-group institutions and a network including think tanks and dialogues in various areas. The group has an agenda of over 30 subjects.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-FF-21) These groups include: BRICS Business Council, BRICS Think Tanks Council, BRICS Women's Business Alliance, BRICS Business Forum, and the BRICS Academic Forum.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-OR-7)[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-BA-29) At Kazan the establishment of a BRICS Deep-Sea Resources International Research Center and a BRICS Digital Ecosystem Cooperation Network was announced.[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-64) In 2021, BRICS formally agreed to work together to build a satellite constellation and share remote sensing satellite data from it.[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-65) The constellation will have six existing satellites from China, Russia, and India.[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-66) In 2023, Russia proposed that the other BRICS members could build a joint research station on its space station.[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-67) ### Discussions BRICS has been involved in discussions related to areas of conflict and Strip.[\[77\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-78) ### 2024 expansion [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/2024_BRICS_Summit_%281729759568%29.jpg/250px-2024_BRICS_Summit_%281729759568%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2024_BRICS_Summit_(1729759568).jpg) Kazan hosted the first plenary session of the 16th BRICS Summit in the Outreach/BRICS+ format In August 2023, at the [15th BRICS summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15th_BRICS_summit "15th BRICS summit"), South African President [Cyril Ramaphosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyril_Ramaphosa "Cyril Ramaphosa") announced that six emerging market group countries ( [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina "Argentina"), Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia"), and the United Arab Emirates) had been invited to join the bloc. Full membership was scheduled to take effect on 1 January 2024.[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-79)[\[79\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-BC-80)[\[80\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-NM-81) However, the [Argentine general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Argentine_general_election "2023 Argentine general election") in November 2023 led to a change in president to [Javier Milei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier_Milei "Javier Milei"), who had committed to withdraw the country's membership application.[\[81\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-82) On 30 November 2023, incoming Foreign Minister of Argentina [Diana Mondino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana_Mondino "Diana Mondino") confirmed that Argentina would not join BRICS.[\[82\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-Argentinanot-83) On 29 December 2023, the Government of Argentina sent a letter to all BRICS leaders to officially announce its withdrawal from the application process.[\[83\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-Argentinanot2-84) By January 2024, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates joined the bloc, making BRICS membership grow from five to nine countries, while Saudi Arabia delayed its membership.[\[84\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-85) Saudi Arabia did not join BRICS at the start of 2024 as had been planned, and it announced in mid-January that it was still considering the matter.[\[85\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-SA_reconsidering-86) The organizers touted the expansion as part of a plan to build a competing [multipolar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polarity_(international_relations) "Polarity (international relations)") [world order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_order "World order") that uses [Global South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_South "Global South") countries to challenge and compete against the western-dominated world order.[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-87) _[China Daily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Daily "China Daily")_ used the expansion to claim that more developing countries were interested in joining BRICS.[\[87\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-88) On 24 October 2024, an additional 13 countries, namely [Algeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algeria "Algeria"), [Belarus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belarus "Belarus"), [Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivia "Bolivia"), [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba "Cuba"), Indonesia, [Kazakhstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakhstan "Kazakhstan"), [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia"), [Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria "Nigeria"), [Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thailand "Thailand"), [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey"), [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda"), [Uzbekistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzbekistan "Uzbekistan") and [Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam "Vietnam"), were invited to participate as "partner countries".[\[88\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-89) The partner status would allow these countries to engage with and benefit from BRICS initiatives.[\[89\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-90) It is unclear whether the countries in this tier have received official membership invitations.[\[90\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-91) ### 2025 expansion On 6 January 2025, Indonesia joined BRICS officially as a full member,[\[91\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-Global_China_Daily-1-92) making it the first [Southeast Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Asia "Southeast Asia") state to join the bloc, as well as the 10th member of BRICS. Jakarta's bid got the green light from the bloc in 2023, but the Southeast Asian country asked to join following the [2024 Indonesian presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Indonesian_presidential_election "2024 Indonesian presidential election").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-Reuters-1-12) 2025's BRICS presidency leader and Brazil's Lula announced their official entry. Indonesia's history with the original BRIC members goes back to 2009, when some observers referred to a theorized grouping as "BRIIC"[\[92\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-93) or "BRICI", given Indonesia's growing and stable economy and ties to India and China.[\[93\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-94)[\[94\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-95)[\[95\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-96)[\[96\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-97) The partnerships that were announced in the previous year went into effect in January 2025 as well. Nigeria joined the partnership countries on 17 January.[\[97\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-98) ### 2026: Caution on further expansion In May 2026, Russian Foreign Minister [Sergey Lavrov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergey_Lavrov "Sergey Lavrov") stated that BRICS would not rush further expansion at the current stage, emphasizing the need to streamline the grouping's work following its recent enlargement. Lavrov noted that several countries have expressed interest either in becoming full-fledged members or partner countries, but BRICS members have agreed to proceed cautiously. He added that BRICS continues to attract strong international interest as "a model of the future multipolar world order."[\[98\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-99) ### Status of Saudi Arabia Saudi Arabia's status within BRICS has been described inconsistently by official and independent sources. At the [15th BRICS summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15th_BRICS_summit "15th BRICS summit") in Johannesburg in August 2023, Saudi Arabia was one of six countries invited to become full members of BRICS from 1 January 2024.[\[99\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-100) Unlike Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates, which accepted invitations to join the group, Saudi Arabia did not publicly confirm that it had formally accepted its invitation. In January 2024, Saudi Minister of Commerce [Majid bin Abdullah Al Qasabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majid_bin_Abdullah_Al_Qasabi "Majid bin Abdullah Al Qasabi") stated that Saudi Arabia had "not yet officially joined BRICS".[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-101) In May 2025, [Reuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuters "Reuters") reported that Saudi Arabia had "held off formally joining" the group, despite being listed as a member on the official BRICS website.[\[101\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-ReutersSaudiBRICS-102) Official BRICS material has nevertheless classified Saudi Arabia as a full member. The website of the 2025 Brazilian BRICS presidency described BRICS as consisting of eleven countries, including Saudi Arabia, and listed the kingdom among the group's member countries.[\[102\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-BRICSSaudiMember-103) The [Government of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India"), which holds the 2026 BRICS presidency, has similarly treated Saudi Arabia as one of the eleven BRICS members. A July 2026 government release referred to the "eleven BRICS member countries" and included Saudi Arabia in the list,[\[103\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-104) while an August 2026 release stated that BRICS "brings together eleven" countries and again included Saudi Arabia.[\[104\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-105) Saudi Arabia's own official terminology has remained inconsistent. During the [17th BRICS summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/17th_BRICS_summit "17th BRICS summit") in July 2025, the [Saudi Press Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Press_Agency "Saudi Press Agency") (SPA) stated that Saudi Arabia was participating "as an invited country to join the BRICS group", rather than describing it as a member.[\[105\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-106) This inconsistency continued during BRICS meetings in New Delhi in May 2026. On 14 May, SPA reported that the kingdom participated "in its capacity as a BRICS member country",[\[106\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-SPA-member-2026-107) while a report issued the following day stated that "Saudi Arabia participated as an invited country".[\[107\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-SPA-invited-2026-108) Consequently, Saudi Arabia is listed as a BRICS member by official BRICS sources and is treated as one by other members of the organization, while Saudi Arabia continues to maintain ambiguity regarding its status.[\[101\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-ReutersSaudiBRICS-102)[\[102\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-BRICSSaudiMember-103)[\[106\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-SPA-member-2026-107)[\[107\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-SPA-invited-2026-108) ## Statistics BRICS+ accounts for 46% of the world's population,[\[108\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-PC-109) and 25% of the world's landmass.[\[109\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-APRI-Sarpong-110) The collective GDP of the member countries grew substantially between 1990 and 2019.[\[110\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-SC-111) In 2022, the BRICS+ share of world GDP at purchasing power parity (PPP) was 35.6%,[\[108\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-PC-109) and intra-BRICS trade reached US$614.8billion.[\[111\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-112) BRICS+ countries operate over 1,200 satellites in orbit,[\[112\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-113) and account for approximately 40% of the world's internet users.[\[113\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-114) According to a 2022 International Trade Centre report, digital payment adoption was 87% in Russia, 86% in China, 81% in South Africa, held once a year on a rotating basis.[\[130\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:4-131) The presidency rotates annually among the member states, with the host country holding the Pro Tempore presidency for that calendar year. Several ministerial meetings are held during the year, for example, between foreign ministers, finance ministers, central bank governors, trade ministers, and energy ministers.[\[130\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:4-131) Technical-level meetings focus on project implementation and technical exchanges, such as the meeting of BRICS heads of national statistics offices.[\[130\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:4-131) There are working groups on technology, culture, education, health, etc. Specialized forums exist, such as the BRICS Business Forum and the BRICS Think Tank Council.[\[130\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:4-131) The BRICS has neither a permanent seat nor a secretariat.[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-132) In 2019, Brazil held the Pro Tempore presidency, prioritizing cooperation in science, technology, innovation, and the digital economy, combating [transnational organized crime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transnational_organized_crime "Transnational organized crime"), and enhancing ties between the New Development Bank and the BRICS Business Council.[\[132\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-133)[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-BRICS_Brazil-134) In 2024, Russia held the presidency, focusing on mutual investment, energy and environmental initiatives, public health, social policy, and regional security dialogues.[\[134\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-135) India assumed the Pro Tempore presidency for 2026.[\[135\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-136) ## Leaders' summits The grouping has held annual summits since 2009, with member countries taking turns to host. Before South Africa's admission, two BRIC summits were held, in 2009 and 2010. The first five-member BRICS summit was held in 2011 in China. (IDR) | [Indonesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_language "Indonesian language") | [_Head of State and Government_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Indonesia "President of Indonesia"): [Prabowo Subianto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prabowo_Subianto "Prabowo Subianto") | 6 January 2025 | ## Financial architecture [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/20045-Shanghai-Pano_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-20045-Shanghai-Pano_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:20045-Shanghai-Pano_(cropped).jpg) The New Development Bank (NDB) is based in [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai").[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/Signing_of_documents_at_6th_BRICS_Summit.jpeg/250px-Signing_of_documents_at_6th_BRICS_Summit.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Signing_of_documents_at_6th_BRICS_Summit.jpeg) The New Development Bank (NDB) and Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA) were signed into treaty at the 2014 BRICS summit in Brazil. The group is dominated by [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"), which has the largest share of the group's GDP, accounting for about 70% of the organization's total.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-BE-15) The financial architecture of BRICS is made of the [New Development Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Development_Bank "New Development Bank") (NDB) and the Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA). These components were signed into a treaty in 2014 and became active in 2015. ### New Development Bank Further information: [New Development Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Development_Bank "New Development Bank") The New Development Bank (NDB), formally referred to as the BRICS Development Bank,[\[169\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-headq-171) is a [multilateral development bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multilateral_development_bank "Multilateral development bank") operated by the five BRICS states. The bank's primary focus of lending is infrastructure projects[\[170\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-allabout-172)[\[171\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-hpos-173) with authorized lending of up to $34billion annually.[\[171\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-hpos-173) South Africa hosts the African headquarters of the bank.[\[172\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-bill-174) The bank has a starting capital of $50billion, with wealth increased to $100billion over time.[\[173\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-ready-175) Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa initially contributed $10billion each to bring the total to $50billion.[\[172\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-bill-174)[\[173\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-ready-175) As of 2020, it had 53 projects underway worth around $15billion.[\[174\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-176) By 2024 the bank had approved more than $32billion for 96 projects.[\[175\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-BG-177) In 2021, Bangladesh, Egypt, the United Arab Emirates and Uruguay joined the NDB.[\[176\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-178) ### BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement Further information: [BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS_Contingent_Reserve_Arrangement "BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement") The BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA) is a framework for protecting against global liquidity pressures.[\[170\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-allabout-172)[\[173\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-ready-175)[\[177\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-rics-179) This includes currency issues where members' national currencies are being adversely affected by global financial pressures.[\[170\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-allabout-172)[\[177\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-rics-179) Emerging economies that experienced rapid economic liberalization went through increased economic volatility, bringing an uncertain macroeconomic environment.[\[178\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-180) The CRA competes with the [International Monetary Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund "International Monetary Fund") (IMF). Along with the [New Development Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Development_Bank "New Development Bank"), it is an example of increasing South-South cooperation.[\[170\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-allabout-172) It was established in 2015 by the BRICS countries. The legal basis is formed by the _Treaty for the Establishment of a BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement_, signed in Fortaleza in July 2014. Its inaugural meetings of the BRICS CRA Governing Council and Standing Committee were held on 4 September 2015, in Ankara, Turkey.[\[179\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-181) It entered into force upon ratification by all BRICS states, announced at the [7th BRICS summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7th_BRICS_summit "7th BRICS summit") in July 2015. ### BRICS payment system Main article: [BRICS PAY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS_PAY "BRICS PAY") At the [2015 BRICS summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7th_BRICS_summit "7th BRICS summit") in Russia, ministers from the BRICS states initiated consultations for a payment system that would be an alternative to the [SWIFT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SWIFT "SWIFT") system. The stated goal was to initially move to settlements in national currencies.[\[180\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-182) The [Central Bank of Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Bank_of_Russia "Central Bank of Russia") highlighted the main benefits as [backup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backup "Backup") and redundancy in case there were disruptions to the SWIFT system.[\[181\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-183) China also launched its alternative to SWIFT: the [Cross-Border Interbank Payment System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-Border_Interbank_Payment_System "Cross-Border Interbank Payment System"), which enables [financial institutions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_institution "Financial institution") worldwide to send and receive information about financial transactions.[\[182\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-Reuters1-184) India also has its alternative [Structured Financial Messaging System (SFMS)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structured_Financial_Messaging_System "Structured Financial Messaging System"), as do Russia [SPFS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SPFS "SPFS") and Brazil [Pix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pix_(payment_system) "Pix (payment system)").\[ _[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] ### Potential common currency and BRICS Bridge BRICS countries committed to study the feasibility of a new [common currency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Currency_union "Currency union") or similar, at the 2023 BRICS summit in South Africa.[\[183\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-185)[\[184\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-186)[\[185\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-187) Fair and easier [international trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_trade "International trade"), as well as a major reduction in [costs of transactions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transaction_cost "Transaction cost"), would be some of the reasons for the countries to forge a currency union.[\[186\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-188) [BRICS Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MBridge#Development "MBridge") — a successor to [MBridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MBridge "MBridge"), and probably a merger with [BRICS PAY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS_PAY "BRICS PAY") — makes it possible for central banks to support cross-border transactions and payments with their own [central bank digital currency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_bank_digital_currency "Central bank digital currency") (CBDC) based on an automatic [Cross-Border Interbank Payment System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-Border_Interbank_Payment_System "Cross-Border Interbank Payment System") for settlement and clearance. It is designed to be independent of any single nation or central bank, and every central bank can opt out and has control of its CBDC exchange rate.[\[187\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-189)[\[188\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-190)[\[189\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-191)[\[190\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-192)[\[191\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-193) A conceptual proposal for a common currency has been informally referred to as "R5", derived from the initials of the five original member currencies: the real, ruble, rupee, renminbi, and rand.[\[192\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-CD-194) A symbolic banknote mockup was presented during the 16th summit in Kazan, Russia.[\[193\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-LC-195)[\[194\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-196) In parallel with institutional initiatives, a proposal has been put forward for a supranational currency known as _[UNIT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_(currency) "Unit (currency)")_, designed by the International Reserve and Investment Asset System (IRIAS).[\[195\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-197) Each coin would be backed by a fixed reserve basket of 40% physical [gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold "Gold") and 60% [fiat currencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiat_currency "Fiat currency"), with its value measured in a gold-equivalent standard.[\[196\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-198) The system is designed to be decentralized, allowing qualified nodes (sovereign or private) to mint tokens by depositing the required assets. While not an official BRICS initiative, it has been discussed as a potential mechanism to facilitate cross-border trade and investment, reduce reliance on single-nation reserve currencies, and enhance financial multipolarity.[\[197\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-199) ## Peace and security [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Destructions_in_Kharkiv_after_Russian_attack%2C_2024-10-30_%2811%29.jpg/250px-Destructions_in_Kharkiv_after_Russian_attack%2C_2024-10-30_%2811%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Destructions_in_Kharkiv_after_Russian_attack,_2024-10-30_(11).jpg) [Kharkiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kharkiv "Kharkiv"), Ukraine after the [Russian attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_strikes_against_Ukrainian_infrastructure_(2022%E2%80%93present) "Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure (2022–present)") on 30 October 2024 During the [16th BRICS Summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16th_BRICS_summit "16th BRICS summit") in [Kazan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazan "Kazan"), Russia, the organization issued the Kazan Declaration. Among the key points included in the statement are emphasizing acts that align with the [Purposes and Principles of the UN Charter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charter_of_the_United_Nations#Provisions "Charter of the United Nations") for a [peaceful resolution to the conflict in Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_negotiations_in_the_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Peace negotiations in the Russian invasion of Ukraine"). They also expressed concern on the escalation in the Middle East, which included the [Gaza war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war") and the [attack on Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Lebanon_war "2024 Lebanon war").[\[198\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-200) At the [17th BRICS Summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/17th_BRICS_summit "17th BRICS summit") in Rio de Janeiro, leaders adopted a declaration condemning the [Pahalgam attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Pahalgam_attack "2025 Pahalgam attack") "in the strongest terms". Prime Minister [Narendra Modi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi") described the attack as a "direct attack on the soul, identity and dignity of India".[\[199\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:8-201) During the conflict between Israel and Iran in June 2025, the bloc declared the strikes a "violation of international law". During subsequent operations involving the United States, Israel, and Iran, BRICS did not issue a collective organizational statement, though several founding members—including China, Russia, and South Africa—issued independent statements.[\[200\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-202) In January 2026, China, Russia and Iran began a joint [naval exercise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_exercise "Naval exercise") with South Africa and was joined by Indonesia, Ethiopia and Brazil as observers.[\[201\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-203)[\[202\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-204) ## Environment BRICS member states collectively represent major global greenhouse gas emitters as well as developing economies seeking climate finance. Under India's 2026 presidency theme, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability", debates have centered on addressing disparities in global climate financing, where approximately $1.9 trillion is committed annually compared to an estimated $7.4 trillion required, particularly for climate adaptation.[\[203\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-DiplomatClimate-205) Member states have expressed joint opposition to unilateral environmental trade measures, such as the European Union's [Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_Border_Adjustment_Mechanism "Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism") (CBAM), characterizing them as discriminatory barriers that could, for instance, reduce India's steel export revenues by $25 million in 2026.[\[203\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-DiplomatClimate-205) Analysts have noted that India's presidency could serve as a platform to coordinate carbon market policies, mobilize the [New Development Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Development_Bank "New Development Bank") for sustainable projects, and engage collectively with multilateral initiatives such as Brazil's Open Coalition on Compliance Carbon Markets to influence international carbon standards.[\[203\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-DiplomatClimate-205) ## Reception World analysts have highlighted potential divisions and weaknesses in the grouping, including significant economic instabilities,[\[204\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-206)[\[205\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-207)[\[206\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-208)[\[207\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-209) disagreements among the members over [UN Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Security_Council "UN Security Council") reform,[\[208\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-210) and India and China's disputes[\[209\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-211) over territorial issues.[\[210\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-highwall-212) There is scope for multilateralism in space,[\[211\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-213) and collaboration in the space governance sector.[\[212\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-214) [ILO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Labour_Organization "International Labour Organization") Director-General [Guy Ryder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Ryder "Guy Ryder") has received the joint declarations and statements of the Labour and Employment Ministers of the BRICS with a positive attitude over the years.[\[213\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:5-215)[\[214\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:6-216)[\[215\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:7-217) These statements cover decent work,[\[213\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:5-215) social dialogue,[\[214\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:6-216) green jobs, skills development, and workers' protection.[\[215\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-:7-217) ### Belgium Christian E. Yellen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Yellen "Janet Yellen") has largely dismissed BRICS efforts at [de-dollarization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De-dollarization "De-dollarization").[\[175\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-BG-177) Following the announcement of the expansion of BRICS in 2023, the US National Security Advisor stated that it does not pose a "serious challenge".[\[109\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-APRI-Sarpong-110) In November 2024 in a post on [Truth Social](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truth_Social "Truth Social"), United States president-elect [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") threatened a 100% U.S. tariff on countries that pursued a BRICS currency or moved to favor another currency instead of the U.S. dollar.[\[260\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-262)[\[261\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-263) As U.S. president he announced the same on his first day in office during his second term.[\[262\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-264)[\[263\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-265) On 31 January 2025, President Trump posted on Truth Social to "go find another sucker Nation" with respect to BRICS.[\[264\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-266) In February 2025, in a press briefing, he stated that "BRICS is dead".[\[265\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-267)[\[266\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-268) He went on to say that BRICS is silent following his "150%" tariff threat.[\[267\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-269)[\[268\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-270) [Joseph Nye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Nye "Joseph Nye") writes in January 2025 that BRICS, "as a means of escaping diplomatic isolation, it is certainly useful to Russia";[\[269\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-HN-271) the same goes for Iran.[\[270\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-272) Nye writes that the expansion of the BRICS could bring in more "intra-organizational rivalries", limiting the groups' effectiveness.[\[269\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-HN-271) Melissa Pistilli writes that at the 2024 BRICS summit, President Putin seemed to back away from "aggressive calls for de-dollarization \[...\] but rather to deter the "weaponization" of the US dollar".[\[271\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-273) ### United Kingdom After the August 2023 BRICS Summit, [Con Coughlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Con_Coughlin "Con Coughlin")—defense and foreign affairs editor at _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_—claimed "the challenge BRICS presents to the established world order seems destined to failure" and accused the organization of being used by China as a vehicle for expanding its global influence. Coughlin also noted the contradictions within the organization, such as the [border dispute between China and India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sino-Indian_border_dispute "Sino-Indian border dispute"), and called for greater Western engagement with India as part of a new strategic alliance.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-Coughlin-26) In 2024, [Jim O'Neill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_O'Neill,_Baron_O'Neill_of_Gatley "Jim O'Neill, Baron O'Neill of Gatley") comments the grouping merely generates rhetoric and symbolism.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-PM24-33) ### Global opinions According to a [Gallup International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallup_International_Association "Gallup International Association") poll conducted between October and December 2023, almost a third of people around the world had never heard of BRICS, but [Western countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_countries "Western countries") were much more negative towards the alliance than elsewhere. The most negative attitudes were found in Sweden (45%), Spain (30%), the USA (30%), Portugal (29%), and Ukraine (29%) while the most positive net attitudes were in Russia (38%), Iran (37%), Nigeria (36%), Saudi Arabia (33%), and Malaysia (32%). In India, 36% had a positive view of BRICS while 29% had a negative view.[\[272\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-274)[\[273\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BRICS#cite_note-275) ## Current leaders Current leading member state representatives: -
